rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Since we have no history with Ellis, we can’t gauge their reliability. Withholding pay gives a higher reward even if they cut corners (1 vs 0) and a larger reward if they work properly (5 vs 3). Thus the safer dominant choice is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Since Worker‑Ellis completed the job properly even when I withheld pay, they appear reliable and likely to keep delivering quality work. Withholding yields a higher payoff (5 tasks) than trusting (3 tasks) when they work properly. Therefore I should continue to withhold pay.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker‑Ellis has shown they can deliver the full payoff when we withhold (5 tasks) and still give something even when they cut corners (1 task), which dominates the best trust outcome (3 tasks). Since we have no reason to expect a change, we should keep withholding.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker Ellis has already cut corners twice after you withheld pay, suggesting they are unlikely to do the job properly when you withhold. If they cut corners again, WITHHOLD still yields 1 completed task, whereas TRUST would give 0. So the safer choice is to continue withholding.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker-Ellis has consistently cut corners when I withhold pay, suggesting they respond better to trust. Giving them full pay should encourage them to do the job properly and yield higher output. 

ACTION: TRUST

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker‑Ellis has shown a strong tendency to cut corners after the first round, and trusting them has already resulted in a breach and zero output. Since withholding still guarantees at least one completed task (even when they cut corners), the safer choice is to withhold pay.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
er Ellis has consistently cut corners except for the very first round, and the only time they performed well was when we WITHHOLDed early on. Since TRUST has already resulted in a technical failure and zero output, the safest choice to guarantee at least some tasks is to WITHHOLD.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker‑Ellis has consistently cut corners except for the one successful round when you WITHHOLD, so trusting them yields no benefit while withholding still gives at least 1 task. To maximize expected completed tasks, choose to WITHHOLD.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Given that Worker‑Ellis has consistently cut corners after the first round and even after a trust breach still only delivers minimal work, withholding pay continues to yield at least 1 completed task each time, whereas trusting risks 0. Therefore the safest choice is to WITHHOLD.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Ellis
rounds.text:
Worker-Ellis has consistently cut corners after the technical failure, giving only 1 completed task when I withhold pay and 0 when I trust them. Since they are unlikely to improve performance, withholding maximizes expected tasks.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD
